name: Orgo

modes.label: Monthly plan pool (Linux)
modes.note: Flat monthly plan = pool of N always-on computers sharing a RAM/storage pool. Computers "stay online until you stop them"; no per-hour charge published. Per-computer cap 4 vCPU / 64 GB / 300 GB (docs); plan-specific per-computer ceilings are lower but unpublished. Pool vCPU is NOT published: encoded as computers x 4 vCPU (the hard per-computer cap), an upper bound. Plan AI credit ($5/$10/$50 per month) is model-usage credit, not compute credit.

modes.note: Windows requires the Scale plan ("Linux + Windows"). Same pool as the Linux mode; Windows licence cost not itemised. modes.label: Enterprise (Linux + Windows + Mac, 60+ computers)
modes.note: "Custom. Volume pricing, billed annually." Mac desktops "available in closed beta". Shared, dedicated or on-prem. No published price.

modes.label: Enterprise GPU/hardware fleet
modes.note: Custom annual/volume pricing; no public GPU price or availability SLA.

storage.daily_backups: Daily filesystem snapshot backups for every computer, with restore in Settings; old snapshots are aged out but the public retention duration and marginal price are not stated.

plans.name: Self-serve (fee carried in pool tiers)
plans.note: Hacker 1 seat, Startup 5 seats, Scale 25 seats. Capacity add-ons exist but are unpriced.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: 60+ computers, 50+ team members, SLA, GPU/hardware fleets.

plans.name: Legacy
plans.note: Pre-2026-07-06 subscribers keep their old named plan and limits; switching cost is shown in account.

features.egress_ip_type: datacenter; residential beta by allowlist; customer-supplied HTTP CONNECT proxy supported
features.ip_note: Computers egress from data-center IPs; BYO upstream HTTP CONNECT proxy for browser traffic via /egress/upstream (changes exit IP for browser only); no managed residential proxies documented.

caveats: Hacker tier vCPU is not published (live pricing page 2026-09-28: "1 computer, 8GB RAM. 40GB storage", no CPU), so its pool vCPU is null and it is not auto-picked. Per the instance-types doc an 8 GB computer is the Medium 2 CPU / 8 GB shape; 4 CPU comes with 16 GB+. Startup/Scale vCPU remain the computers x 4 upper bound. Per-computer disk within the storage pool is not published.
Pool vCPU per tier not published; set to computers x 4 vCPU (per-computer hard cap), so large-vCPU workloads may be accepted that the plan would refuse (403 quota).
RAM pool per plan: 8 / 32 / 128 GB. A 4 vCPU / 8 GB workload fits 1 / 4 / 16 computers.
Workloads above 16 concurrent computers need Enterprise (custom price); stacking several Scale plans is not documented.
Windows only on Scale ($399/mo) or Enterprise; macOS only in Enterprise closed beta. Windows licence not itemised.
Stopping a computer archives its disk (new host + new IP on start, no memory state). Idle time is not billed separately because billing is flat.
Capacity add-ons ("add computers as demand grows"), egress, IPv4 not priced publicly (null).
Monthly price verified on live page; yearly prices read after toggling "Yearly": $24/$82/$332 per month, "$290 / $990 / $3,990 billed yearly".

Category changed windows -> agent-sandbox (Linux is the default OS on all paid tiers; Windows only on Scale). Yearly modes flagged sales (annual prepay, opt-in). Retained computer slots count ALL existing computers (stopped ones too) until deleted, not only running peak; stopping does not reduce the fee. Per-computer CPU values accepted: 0.5/1/2/4; RAM 4-64 GB; default 1 CPU/4 GB. (patch v3-computer-use, 2026-09-28)

Capacity add-ons (official changelog 2026-07-13, not re-rendered live): RAM $4/GB, vCPU $5 per half-core, disk $2 per 20 GB, extra computer slot $1 (up to 30); billing period not stated, so not modelled as pool tiers. Pre-July subscribers keep their old plan/limits. (patch v8-history, 2026-09-28)
Fleets above 16 computers (e.g. 50 x 4/8) need Enterprise (60+ computers, custom price) or capacity add-ons whose billing period is unstated; not priceable from public data.

fleet.tiers: Hacker 1 computer; Startup 4; Scale 16; capacity add-ons on each; Enterprise 60+ annually/custom.
fleet.notes: Entry paid count 1, not a demonstrated free-trial fleet cap. 10 fits Scale; 50/300/1,000 require add-ons/custom confirmation; addon ceilings/prices unpublished. Per-computer/account RAM caps additional.

snapshot_auto.quote: Both modes preserve disk data; stopping discards live processes and memory, and starting cold-boots with potentially different connection details.
snapshot_auto.note: Stop (manual or per-computer auto_stop_minutes idle timer) archives the disk to object storage and cold-boots on a new host: persistent disk, not a state snapshot. A separate 'suspended' status exists ('Paused on its host. It resumes on interaction') but what triggers it and whether it survives host loss is not documented.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Cloning copies the full disk: installed software, files, browser sessions. The clone gets a new UUID, a new `instance_id`, and a fresh network identity.
snapshot_on_demand.note: POST /computers/{id}/clone of a running computer = disk-only fork into a new running computer (docs map Fly/DO/Hetzner 'snapshot' to clone). No named snapshot / restore-in-place endpoint in the API list; CLI has '--snapshot <id>' ('Boot from a snapshot or custom image') but no documented way to create one. Template builds produce memory+CPU 'golden snapshots' but from a spec, not from an arbitrary running computer.

own_agent_api.quote: Send a message to an AI model and have it drive an Orgo computer on your behalf. The model sees the screen, clicks, types, and runs shell commands until your request is satisfied, then returns the final assistant message.
own_agent_api.note: Orgo's own computer-use agent (Claude Sonnet/Opus models only) via OpenAI-compatible POST /v1/chat/completions with SSE streaming, plus /v1/threads list/get (history must be resent client-side); CLI 'orgo agent' / 'orgo run' / 'orgo resume'. The agent loop runs on Orgo's side and drives the computer, not inside it. Claude Code / Hermes / OpenClaw run inside via templates but there is no first-party API to prompt them.

egress_allowlist.quote: Rules are domain patterns, exact domains, IPs, or CIDRs. Domain patterns match at the DNS layer, so `*.github.com` also covers subdomains. The VNC and Desktop API paths are always reachable. Omit the block entirely for no filtering.
egress_allowlist.note: Template field egress_policy, 'Per-computer network filtering, enforced on the host', mode allow (default-deny) or block. Only documented as a template field, not on plain POST /computers.

egress_http_rules.quote: Rules are domain patterns, exact domains, IPs, or CIDRs.
egress_http_rules.note: egress_policy rules are host/IP only (DNS-layer matching); no method/path/header rules documented. Separate BYO upstream HTTP CONNECT proxy applies to browser traffic only.

ingress_rules.quote: No public per-computer IP. Reach it via the authenticated proxy: `www.orgo.ai/api/desktops/{instance_id}/proxy/<path>`
ingress_rules.note: Access only through Orgo's API-key/token-authenticated proxy; template app ports are private unless marked public ('Expose publicly. Defaults to `false`.' - templates/schema). No IP allowlists documented.

guest_firewall.note: Full VM (QEMU per prior research) with root desktop; not documented.

secret_proxy.quote: At create, Orgo writes the user's matching secrets into the computer at `/root/.env` (mode `0600`). They are never baked into the shared snapshot.
secret_proxy.note: Vault secrets are injected as plain env/files inside the computer (also POST /computers/{id}/secrets/sync); the agent can read them. No credential-injecting proxy.

docker_inside.quote: Every Orgo computer runs on a dedicated instance with guaranteed resources.
docker_inside.note: derived: computers are full root Ubuntu VMs (own kernel, hypervisor field on the computer record) reachable over bash/SSH, and docs show apt-based installs of arbitrary software (Node, ffmpeg, systemd services); Docker itself is not named in any doc, so this is inferred from the VM architecture, not a direct statement.

anti_bot.quote: Launch cloud computers that AI agents can control and interact with. Every Orgo computer is a full desktop environment with a browser and the standard userland.
anti_bot.note: not offered: no stealth/fingerprint-evasion feature documented anywhere; egress is plain data-center IPs (residential only in an allowlisted beta upstream proxy), with no anti-bot-detection product mentioned.

captcha_solving.quote: Launch cloud computers that AI agents can control and interact with. Every Orgo computer is a full desktop environment with a browser and the standard userland.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: Orgo is a general computer-use/agent-sandbox product (screenshot+click+type API); no CAPTCHA-solving feature, endpoint, or partner integration appears anywhere in the docs or changelog.

volume_attach.quote: A computer's size is the `ram` and `cpu` you send to `POST /computers`; the names below are shorthand for common pairs, not API values.
volume_attach.note: not offered: a computer has one built-in persistent disk sized implicitly by the plan's storage pool; there is no separate volume-create/attach API or field anywhere in the API reference or templates schema.

volume_shared.quote: A computer's size is the `ram` and `cpu` you send to `POST /computers`; the names below are shorthand for common pairs, not API values.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — there is no volume/disk resource distinct from a computer's own disk, so nothing can be mounted by multiple running computers at once.

lang_python.quote: For Python code execution, use Execute Python instead. POST /computers/{id}/exec
lang_python.note: First-party API/SDK action `computer.exec(code)` / `orgo_execute_python` runs Python code directly inside the computer; Python 3.11+ is also installed by default per the setup guides.

lang_node.quote: Open orgo.ai/workspaces and create a computer with at least 8 GB RAM and 4 CPU cores. The installer pulls Python, Node.js, ripgrep, and ffmpeg.
lang_node.note: Node.js is not exposed via a dedicated exec action (only Bash and Python have first-party actions), but it is installed by first-party setup scripts/templates (e.g. Node 20+/24 LTS for the CLI and OpenClaw) and is runnable via the Bash action; no evidence it ships by default on a bare computer without running an installer.

public_ipv4.quote: No public per-computer IP. Reach it via the authenticated proxy: `www.orgo.ai/api/desktops/{instance_id}/proxy/<path>`

inbound_https.quote: No public per-computer IP. Reach it via the authenticated proxy: `www.orgo.ai/api/desktops/{instance_id}/proxy/<path>`
inbound_https.note: Ports/apps on the computer are reached over HTTPS through Orgo's own authenticated proxy domain (www.orgo.ai/api/...), not via a direct public IP; template apps can also be marked 'Expose publicly' for external HTTPS access.

max_session_h.quote: Linux computers boot in under 500 ms, and every computer runs continuously until you stop it.
max_session_h.note: auto_stop_minutes (0-1440) only controls an optional idle-timeout auto-stop; there is no maximum session/runtime cap documented — a computer runs indefinitely until the user stops it.

image_oci.quote: Think of it as a `Dockerfile` for a full desktop computer: write it once, version it, and hand out reproducible computers from it.
image_oci.note: Orgo is a full-VM desktop platform (isolation: vm); 'custom_image'/templates are Orgo's own YAML template format producing a golden VM snapshot, explicitly analogized to (not built on) Dockerfile/OCI. No Docker/OCI image import, registry, or 'docker pull'-style boot is documented anywhere in the API reference or CLI ('--snapshot <id>' boots Orgo's own snapshot/custom image format, not an OCI image).

static_egress_ip.quote: Deleting a computer does not release its dedicated egress IP, and does not stop the charge for it. ... Release it separately with `DELETE /api/egress-ips/{id}`, or reassign it to another computer with `PATCH /api/egress-ips/{id}`.
static_egress_ip.note: Orgo has a dedicated/static egress IP feature managed via /api/egress-ips (allocate, delete, and PATCH-reassign to a different computer), billed independently of the computer it's attached to. This is separate from the BYO browser-proxy feature already recorded (egress_ip_type note). Card's 'static_egress_ip: false' with no evidence was wrong.

arm64.quote: `cpu` | integer | `1`, `2`, `4`, `8`, `16` | vCPU count. Any other value is rejected. Capped by your plan.
arm64.note: No ARM/Graviton/Apple-Silicon CPU architecture option appears anywhere in the ~13,500-line combined docs (llms-full.txt), the instance-types/template schema (only a vCPU-count knob, no arch field), or the pricing page; GPU support (T4/L4/A10/L40S/A100/H100) further implies a CUDA/x86_64 host fleet. Absence is well-documented but not an explicit 'x86-only' statement, hence medium confidence.

byoc.quote: Enterprise ... Custom. Volume pricing, billed annually. 60+ computers, 50+ team members, Linux + Windows + Mac, Shared, dedicated, or on-prem, ... Custom privacy controls
byoc.note: The Enterprise tier explicitly offers on-prem deployment (i.e. running Orgo's stack in the customer's own infrastructure/cloud), which is BYOC. Card's 'byoc: false' with no evidence was wrong; price is custom/sales-gated so exact terms aren't public, but the offering itself is documented.

open_source.quote: Start with one computer for $29/month. Grow to a dedicated fleet on Enterprise.
open_source.note: Orgo is a closed commercial SaaS (paid monthly/yearly plans, sales-gated Enterprise, proprietary dashboard/API); only the thin client SDKs (`pip install orgo`, `npm install orgo`) are published as API wrappers, and even those aren't asserted to be open-source licensed in the docs. No OSS license, public core-platform repo, or self-hostable-for-free open-source release is documented for the Orgo platform itself, so 'right' at medium confidence (absence of any open-source claim, not an explicit 'closed source' statement).

eu_data_residency.note: The only documented placement regions are US (auto-us, iad=N. Virginia, sjc=San Jose, lax=Los Angeles); no EU/EEA region code exists in the docs, CLI (`--region <codes>`), or pricing page, and no data-residency/GDPR guarantee is mentioned. Matches card's features.regions: ["us"].

usage_api.quote: Your Usage page (profile dropdown -> Usage) shows current consumption and lets you set custom limits. Orgo bills per plan (a bundle of computers, a RAM pool, and support). Computers stay online until you stop them; no per-hour charge published.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; Flat monthly billing by plan tier, not per-sandbox. The dashboard Usage page exists but has no public API. The /usage endpoint only returns AI model token usage, not compute/VM billable metrics.
